questions.question: One mole is:
options: The mass of one molecule
A fixed number of particles — six comma zero two times ten to the twenty-three
One gram of any substance
The volume of one litre of gas

questions.question: Avogadro's number was fixed at its strange size so that:
options: It would be easy to memorise
All gases would weigh the same
One mole of a substance weighs, in grams, exactly its relative atomic or molecular mass
Calculators could display it exactly

questions.question: Read as a sentence, n equals m over M says:
options: The number of moles equals the mass you have divided by the mass of one mole
Mass equals moles divided by molar mass
Molar mass equals mass times moles
Moles equal molecules divided by mass

subtopics.title: Moles from Mass — the 8,8 Gram Question

questions.question: The molar mass of propane, C3H8, is:
options: 13 grams per mole — one carbon plus one hydrogen
20 grams per mole
56 grams per mole
44 grams per mole — three times twelve plus eight times one

questions.question: The number of moles in 8,8 grams of propane is:
options: 0,2 moles — 8,8 divided by 44
5 moles — 44 divided by 8,8
8,8 moles
0,5 moles

questions.question: The sense-check that catches an upside-down division here is:
options: 0,2 moles is impossible because moles must be whole numbers
Five moles of propane would weigh two hundred and twenty grams, not 8,8 — so 5 moles cannot be right
8,8 grams is always 0,2 moles of any gas
The calculator never inverts a division

subtopics.title: From Moles to Molecules, and to Litres at STP

questions.question: The number of molecules in 0,2 moles of propane is:
options: 6,02 times ten to the twenty-three
0,2 molecules
1,204 times ten to the twenty-three — 0,2 times Avogadro's number
3,01 times ten to the twenty-three

questions.question: Avogadro's law states that at the same temperature and pressure:
options: Heavier gases fill larger volumes
Equal volumes of any gases contain equal numbers of molecules
All gases have the same mass
A mole of gas always fills exactly one litre

questions.question: STP means:
options: Twenty-five degrees Celsius and any pressure
Zero kelvin and one kilopascal
Room temperature and sea-level pressure
Zero degrees Celsius — 273 kelvin — and 101,3 kilopascals

questions.question: The volume of 0,2 moles of propane at STP is:
options: 4,48 cubic decimetres — 0,2 times 22,4
22,4 cubic decimetres
112 cubic decimetres
0,2 cubic decimetres

subtopics.title: The Mole Map — Navigating Every Conversion

questions.question: On the mole map, the direction rule is:
options: Always multiply, whichever way you travel
Travelling out of the centre you multiply; travelling in to moles you divide
Travelling out you divide; travelling in you multiply
Directions depend on the gas involved

questions.question: A question gives the volume of a gas at STP and asks for its mass. The itinerary is:
options: Multiply the volume by the molar mass directly
Divide by Avogadro's number, then multiply by 22,4
In to moles by dividing by 22,4, then out to mass by multiplying by the molar mass
Multiply by 22,4, then divide by the molar mass

questions.question: The 22,4 cubic decimetres per mole shortcut may be used:
options: For any substance at any temperature
For liquids and solids as well as gases
For gases at any pressure
Only for gases, and only at STP

questions.question: One exhibit in the error museum is unit chaos. The correct relationships are:
options: Mass in grams; one thousand cubic centimetres make one cubic decimetre, which is one litre
Mass in kilograms; one hundred cubic centimetres make one cubic decimetre
Mass in grams; one cubic centimetre equals one litre
Mass in milligrams; ten cubic centimetres make one litre

subtopics.title: Nobody Counts Rice Grains — They Count Bags

questions.question: The depot counts bags instead of rice grains because:
options: Bags are worth more than grains
Grains are too small and too many to count one by one — a fixed bag size lets weighing stand in for counting
Rice cannot be weighed directly
Counting grains is illegal at a depot

questions.question: In the bag picture, the periodic table is:
options: A list of bag sizes in litres
A count of the bags in stock
The price list — each element's mass in grams per bag, its molar mass
A recipe book for reactions

questions.question: A mole of hydrogen atoms weighs:
options: One gram — hydrogen's periodic-table number in grams
Twelve grams
Six comma zero two grams
Twenty-two comma four grams

subtopics.title: A Fifth of a Bag of Sugar

questions.question: Reading C3H8 like an invoice gives a bag mass of:
options: 13 grams per mole — one carbon, one hydrogen
20 grams per mole
44 grams per mole — three twelves plus eight ones
36 grams per mole — the carbons only

questions.question: Before touching a calculator, 8,8 divided by 44 must come out as:
options: Five bags, because 44 contains 8,8 five times
A fifth of a bag — 8,8 is one fifth of 44
Exactly one bag
Ten bags

questions.question: Travelling from bags out to particles you always multiply because:
options: Multiplying is faster on a calculator
Avogadro's number is negative
Particles weigh more than bags
Particles are the tiny, numerous thing — the count must come out enormous

questions.question: The number of molecules in the fifth of a bag is:
options: 1,204 times ten to the twenty-three
6,02 times ten to the twenty-three
0,2 times ten to the ten
44 times ten to the twenty-three

subtopics.title: Same Room for Any Gas — and the Rank in the Middle

questions.question: One mole of propane and one mole of hydrogen at the same temperature and pressure fill:
options: Volumes proportional to their molar masses
The same volume — a gas is mostly empty space, so molecule size hardly matters
Very different volumes, because propane is heavier
Volumes that cannot be compared

questions.question: The volume of the leaked propane — 0,2 moles at STP — is:
options: 22,4 litres
0,448 litres
4,48 litres — about two big cooldrink bottles
44,8 litres

questions.question: The twenty-two comma four may NOT be used when:
options: The substance is a gas at exactly 273 kelvin
The question says standard conditions
The gas is propane rather than oxygen
The question gives no STP, or the substance is a liquid or solid

questions.question: In the taxi-rank picture, every mole problem is:
options: One trip — ride in to the rank by dividing, count moles, ride out by multiplying
Three separate formulae with nothing in common
A round trip that always ends at mass
A trip that skips the rank entirely
